chunks: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Imams after the Prophet (may God's blessings be upon him and his family). So he said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) was an Imam, then al-Hasan (peace be upon him) was an Imam, then al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was an Imam, then Ali ibn al-Husayn was an Imam, then Muhammad ibn Ali was an Imam.
Whoever denies that is like one who denies the recognition of God, Blessed and Exalted, and the recognition of His Messenger (may God's blessings be upon him and his family).

Then the narrator said: I said, 'Then you — may I be sacrificed for you!' So I repeated it to him three times. So he said to me: Indeed I have only narrated to you so that you may be among the witnesses of God, Blessed and Exalted, in His earth.

key_terms.أمير المؤمنين: Commander of the Faithful — the title of Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib
key_terms.الأئمة: The Imams — the twelve divinely-appointed successors in Shia belief
key_terms.شهداء الله: Witnesses of God — those entrusted to bear testimony to divine truth on earth
key_terms.معرفة الله: Ma'rifat Allah — recognition/gnosis of God, the highest level of theological knowledge

ai.seo_question: Who are the Imams after the Prophet according to Imam Sadiq in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: In this hadith, Zarih ibn Muhammad al-Muharibi asks Imam Sadiq (AS) about the succession of Imams after the Prophet. The Imam enumerates five Imams — Ali, Hasan, Husayn, Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin), and Muhammad ibn Ali (al-Baqir) — emphasizing that denial of their Imamate is equivalent to denying God Himself and His Prophet. The closing exchange reveals a deeper purpose: the Imam narrated this not merely to inform, but to make his companion a living witness to the doctrine of Imamate on God's earth, reflecting the Shia theological concept of the Imams as guardians of divine knowledge and testimony.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Jamhour, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Muawiya Bin Wahab, from Zareeh who said, 
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the Imams<sup>asws</sup> after the Prophet<sup>saww</sup>. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> was an Imam<sup>asws</sup>, then Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> was an Imam<sup>asws</sup>, and Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> was an Imam<sup>asws</sup>, and Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> was an Imam<sup>asws</sup>, and Muhammad<sup>asws</sup> Bin Ali<sup>asws</sup> was an Imam<sup>asws</sup>.
The one who denies that, he would be like the one who denies the recognition of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High, and recognition of His<sup>azwj</sup> Rasool<sup>saww</sup>’.

Then he (the narrator) said, ‘I said, ‘Then you<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, may I be sacrificed for you<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>!’ So I reiterated it upon him<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> three times. So he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said to me: ‘I<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> rather, narrated to you in order for you to become from the witnesses of Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Blessed and High in His<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> earth’.
en.sarwar: 5. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Jaumhur from Faddala ibn Ayyub from Mu‘awiya ibn Wahab from Dhurayh who has said the following. “I asked abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) about the Imams after the Holy Prophet (s.a.).” The Imam (a.s.) said, “Amir al-Mu’minin (Ali) (a.s.) was the Imam. Then al-Hassan (a.s.) was the Imam. Then al-Husayn (a.s.) was the Imam. Then Ali ibn Al-Husayn (a.s.) was the Imam. Then Muhammad ibn Ali (a.s.) was the Imam.
One who would deny this would be as if he has denied the existence of Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, and the truthfulness of Prophet Muhammad (s.a).

” I asked, “may Allah take my soul in service for your cause, are you then the Imam? I repeated it three times.” The Imam said, “I only said it to you so that you will be of the witnesses before Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, on His earth.”
